newsitem.title: CHINA: China 1996 trade surplus seen at $18 bln.
newsitem.headline: China 1996 trade surplus seen at $18 bln.

text.p: China is expected to enjoy a trade surplus of $18 billion for 1996, up from $16.69 billion in 1995, the official Securities Daily said on Friday.
Exports were expected to rise 3.6 percent to $154 billion and imports were seen to climb 3.0 percent to $136 billion, the newspaper quoted State Planning Commission predictions as showing.
In the second half of the year, trading companies had turned around an earlier fall in the value of exports, and that trend would continue in the remainder of the fourth quarter, it said.
China recorded a trade surplus of $12.01 billion in the first 10 months of this year, the newspaper said, adding that exports have been gaining momentum in recent months, far outpacing imports.
Gross domestic product (GDP) was forecast to grow 9.6 percent, supported by stable expansion of tertiary industry and higher industrial output, the newspaper said.
Industrial output was forecast to grow a year-on-year 11.2 percent in the fourth quarter, it said.
